findings.title: rawTokenId null check is wrong: it re-checks grantType and the message names rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') on line 73, so rawTokenId is never validated and the grantType check is duplicated. A null rawTokenId is accepted, and encodeTokenId() would then build an ID ending in ':null' that is not the generated token id. The check should be on rawTokenId.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId grant-shortcut check is inverted and reads the wrong characters
findings.body: In isAccessTokenId, line 483 returns false when items[0].substring(3, 5) equals the expected grant shortcut. Two things are wrong. The condition is inverted, so a match is rejected. The offsets are also wrong: the token id layout is 2 chars session type, 2 chars token type, then the 2-char grant shortcut at indices 4-5, so the code should read substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). For 'onrtac' the code reads 'ta'. The net effect is that the grant assertion in expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken never fails for a well-formed id, so a regression that issues tokens with the wrong grant shortcut will not be caught. For an id whose prefix is shorter than 5 characters, substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the match. The comment saying the shortcut starts at the '4th char' also does not match the code.

findings.title: Javadoc asks for 3-letter grant shortcuts, but the encoding requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The getShortcut() Javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'. The encoder does not work that way: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId reads the grant shortcut as substring(4, 6) and requires the encoded prefix to be exactly 6 characters. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit only checks uniqueness, not length. A grant implementer who follows this Javadoc returns a 3-character shortcut. encodeTokenId then succeeds and issues a token with a 7-character prefix, but that token id can never be decoded ('Expected length of 6'). The Javadoc should say 2 characters, and postInit (or encodeTokenId) should reject shortcuts of any other length.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks every existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation
findings.body: getShortcut() is added as an abstract method with no default, so every existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation (in extensions, or test-only grant types) stops compiling until it adds the method. The PR does not mention this as a breaking change. The new postInit in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory (around line 72) also casts every OAuth2GrantType factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. A grant registered as a plain ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType> (which the token endpoint dispatch accepts) therefore causes a ClassCastException at server startup. A default method, plus skipping or handling factories that do not provide a shortcut, would avoid both problems.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes on any RuntimeException, including the NPE from a null sessionFactory
findings.body: The test catches RuntimeException and does not check its type. The test factory never sets sessionFactory, so for shortcut 'ac' getGrantTypeByShortcut falls through to sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...) and throws NullPointerException. The test therefore passes without exercising the intended IllegalArgumentException for an unknown grant shortcut, and it would also pass for any other bug. It should assert IllegalArgumentException, with a stubbed session factory if needed.

findings.title: Production path getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext and factory validation are untested
findings.body: The tests only cover string decode/encode round-trips. They do not cover getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, which TokenManager.initToken calls for every access token. That method decides session type (TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE), the lightweight-vs-regular decision, and the fallback to 'na' when the grant attribute is missing. Also untested: the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation, and the refresh branches of getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut. A bug in the code path that fills every issued token id would not be caught by these tests.

findings.title: Access token jti is no longer a UUID for every access token, with no compatibility note
findings.body: initToken now sets the access token jti to a value like 'onrtac:<uuid>' instead of a plain UUID. Any consumer, event listener or client that validates or parses jti as a UUID will break. The PR does not document this as a change to the token format or mention a compatibility impact, and the only test updates are in AssertEvents. This should be called out in the PR description or release notes.

findings.title: Only the standard token-exchange provider records the grant type, so other token-exchange paths encode 'na'
findings.body: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient. Other token-exchange providers that issue access tokens through the same TokenManager responseBuilder path do not set the attribute. Their token ids encode the grant as 'na' (UNKNOWN), even though the grant being served is token-exchange. That undermines the grant-type purpose the PR states for the token-exchange use case. Either set the attribute in every provider that issues tokens, or document the limitation.

findings.title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed without deprecation
findings.body: The public copy constructor Context(Context) is deleted in this PR. The change is unrelated to the feature and is not mentioned in the description. Any external grant implementation that calls it will fail to compile. If the removal is intentional, it should be called out, or the constructor should be kept and deprecated.
